mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 4% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings and consumer spending, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when UNRATE exceeds 4% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when RSAFS declines for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals improving supply capacity, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when INDPRO increases for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in payroll employment above 4% signals robust labor market conditions, which boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when PAYEMS exceeds 4% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strengthening demand, which boosts corporate revenue and profit growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when RSAFS increases for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 4% combined with a 3-month decline in payroll employment signals a severe labor market downturn, which reduces corporate earnings and consumer spending, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 4.0% AND PAYEMS falls for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when both UNRATE exceeds 4% and PAYEMS declines for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
